options.A: Principle 6 - Remuneration
options.B: Principle 12 - Shareholder rights
options.D: Principle 9 - Risk Management

questions.explanation: Under corporate governance guidelines, risk management oversight is a board responsibility captured under the risk management principle (Principle 9). Principle 6 addresses remuneration, Principle 3 the separation of Chairman and CEO roles, and Principle 12 shareholder engagement. Board oversight of risk management is distinct from these other governance areas.

questions.stem: Under MAS Guidelines G16 on Outsourcing, a financial institution that outsources a material activity must ensure which of the following?

options.A: The financial institution retains accountability and oversight of the outsourced activity
options.B: MAS is notified in advance and the outsourcing arrangement is approved by MAS
options.C: The service provider is incorporated in Singapore
options.D: The service provider undergoes a MAS-conducted audit annually

questions.explanation: G16 requires that the financial institution remains accountable for the outsourced activity and maintains oversight. The service provider need not be incorporated in Singapore. MAS notification (not pre-approval) is required for material outsourcing, and MAS does not conduct its own annual audits of service providers as a standard requirement. Accountability and oversight are the core obligations.

questions.stem: Under MAS Guidelines FSG-G02, a financial institution's internal audit function must report to which body to preserve its independence?

options.A: The Chief Executive Officer
options.B: The Audit Committee of the Board
options.D: The Head of Risk Management

questions.explanation: FSG-G02 requires internal audit to report to the Audit Committee of the Board (or equivalent) to ensure it is independent of management. Reporting to the CEO, Compliance Officer, or Head of Risk Management would compromise independence because internal audit is meant to provide objective assurance to the board.

questions.stem: Under the Code on CIS, the trustee of a retail scheme is primarily responsible for:

options.A: Making investment decisions for the scheme
options.B: Marketing and distributing the scheme to retail investors
options.C: Preparing the prospectus for MAS registration
options.D: Safeguarding the assets of the scheme and ensuring the manager complies with the trust deed

questions.explanation: The trustee's role under the Code on CIS is to hold and safeguard scheme assets, act in unitholders' interests, and ensure the scheme manager complies with the trust deed and regulations. Investment decisions are made by the manager. Marketing and distribution are the manager's and distributor's functions. Prospectus preparation is the manager's responsibility.

questions.stem: Under MAS Notice FAA-N06 on AML/CFT, a financial adviser is required to terminate a business relationship in which of the following circumstances?

options.A: The client's income increases significantly, triggering a new risk tier
options.B: The client requests a transfer to a competitor FA firm
options.C: The FA is unable to complete CDD due to the client's refusal to provide required information
options.D: The client has not transacted for more than 12 months

questions.explanation: FAA-N06 requires a financial adviser to terminate (or not establish) a business relationship when the FA is unable to complete the required CDD because the client refuses to provide necessary information. In such cases, the FA should also consider filing an STR. Increased client income, transfers, and inactivity are not grounds for mandatory termination.

questions.stem: Under the Ethics framework, 'moral courage' in the context of a financial adviser means:

options.A: Willingness to challenge the firm's management when ethical standards are being compromised
options.B: Willingness to recommend high-risk products to maximise client returns
options.C: Ability to make quick decisions under time pressure during client meetings
options.D: Confidence in promoting one's own services over competitors

questions.explanation: Moral courage in professional ethics means having the willingness to speak up, challenge, or act when ethical standards are being violated - even when it is personally costly to do so, such as challenging management decisions or reporting misconduct. It is not about risk appetite, decisiveness under pressure, or competitive self-promotion.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the 'suitability' obligation of a financial adviser under the FAA?

options.A: The adviser must recommend only the cheapest product available for each need
options.B: The adviser must recommend only products from the firm's approved product list regardless of the client's needs
options.C: The adviser must recommend products approved by both MAS and the client's employer
options.D: The adviser must have a reasonable basis that the recommendation is appropriate for the client's specific circumstances

questions.explanation: The suitability obligation requires the adviser to have a reasonable basis - grounded in knowing the client's circumstances, needs, risk profile, and objectives - that the recommendation is appropriate for that specific client. It does not mandate the cheapest product, dual approvals, or rigid adherence to an approved list if the product does not suit the client.

questions.stem: Under MAS Notice FAA-N06, which of the following is NOT one of the key elements of Customer Due Diligence (CDD)?

options.A: Identifying the customer and verifying the customer's identity
options.B: Identifying the beneficial owner and verifying the beneficial owner's identity
options.C: Conducting a credit assessment to determine the client's ability to invest
options.D: Understanding the nature and purpose of the business relationship

questions.explanation: CDD under FAA-N06 comprises: (i) identifying and verifying the customer, (ii) identifying and verifying the beneficial owner, (iii) understanding the nature and purpose of the business relationship, and (iv) ongoing monitoring. A credit assessment is a suitability and lending tool, not a CDD requirement under AML/CFT rules.

questions.stem: Under MAS Notice FAA-N06, 'ongoing monitoring' of a business relationship requires which of the following?

options.A: Scrutinising transactions to ensure they are consistent with the FA's knowledge of the client and their source of funds
options.B: Contacting the client once per year by telephone to confirm personal details
options.C: Filing an STR for every transaction above S$5,000
options.D: Reviewing the client's investment portfolio performance quarterly

questions.explanation: Ongoing monitoring under FAA-N06 involves scrutinising transactions conducted throughout the relationship to ensure they are consistent with the FA's understanding of the client, their business, and their source of funds - and to identify any unusual or suspicious activity. Annual telephone calls, STRs for every S$5,000 transaction, and portfolio performance reviews are not the prescribed ongoing monitoring activities.

questions.stem: A representative fails to submit a required MAS regulatory return on time. This is an example of which category of ethical failure?

options.A: Misrepresentation
options.B: Churning
options.C: Negligence or failure to comply with regulatory obligations
options.D: Conflict of interest

questions.explanation: Failing to comply with a regulatory obligation (such as timely submission of required returns) is a failure of professional responsibility and regulatory compliance - classified as negligence or non-compliance. It is distinct from misrepresentation (making false statements), churning (excessive switching), or conflict of interest (personal interest affecting recommendations).

questions.stem: Under the FAA, a licensed financial adviser that conducts regulated activity while its licence is suspended commits an offence. The maximum fine is:
questions.explanation: Conducting regulated activity while a financial adviser's licence is suspended is a serious offence under the FAA, attracting a maximum fine of S$150,000. This is significantly higher than other FAA fines because it involves deliberate operation outside authorised status. S$50,000 is the cap for offences such as permitting unqualified reps. S$25,000 applies to the acting-for-multiple-principals offence.

questions.stem: A licensed financial adviser wishes to hold client assets (e.g. securities and cash) directly. Under the FAA and related regulations, the FA must:

options.A: Obtain separate CMS licence for custodial services
options.B: Segregate client assets from the FA's own assets at all times
options.C: File a client asset notification with MAS monthly
options.D: Obtain written consent from each client before holding their assets

questions.explanation: A licensed FA that holds client assets is required to segregate them from its own assets at all times, to protect clients in the event of the FA's insolvency. Holding client assets does not automatically require a CMS licence if it is incidental to the advisory service. There is no monthly MAS notification or general written consent requirement specifically for asset holding in this context.

questions.stem: Under the concept of fair dealing, 'information asymmetry' between a financial adviser and a client is ethically significant because:

options.A: It allows the FA to charge premium fees that other advisers cannot justify
options.B: It requires the FA to apply a fixed fee structure rather than commission
options.C: It means the FA must seek MAS approval before recommending complex products
options.D: It creates a duty on the FA to share relevant information that the client needs to make informed decisions

questions.explanation: Information asymmetry - where the adviser knows significantly more than the client - creates a fiduciary-like duty to share material information. The ethically correct response is to use that knowledge to serve the client, not to exploit the gap. Information asymmetry does not entitle the FA to premium fees, require MAS pre-approval, or mandate a particular fee structure.

questions.stem: Under the FAA and AML/CFT rules, a 'beneficial owner' is BEST described as:

options.A: The individual whose name appears on the investment account
options.B: The legal trustee acting on behalf of a trust
options.C: The nominee shareholder of the customer company
options.D: The natural person who ultimately owns or controls the customer

questions.explanation: A beneficial owner under FAA-N06 and AML/CFT frameworks is the natural person who ultimately owns or exercises control over the customer, behind any legal or nominee structures. The account holder may be a company or nominee. The nominee shareholder and legal trustee are intermediary structures - the beneficial owner is the ultimate natural person behind them.

questions.stem: Under MAS Notice FAA-N06, which of the following statements about reliance on third-party CDD is correct?

options.A: If CDD is conducted by a third party, the financial adviser bears no further responsibility for the adequacy of that CDD
options.B: The FA may rely on CDD conducted by a group entity that is subject to equivalent AML/CFT supervision
options.C: Third-party CDD reliance is only permitted for institutional clients, never for individuals
options.D: The FA must obtain MAS written approval before relying on any third-party CDD

questions.explanation: FAA-N06 permits reliance on third-party CDD conducted by group entities subject to equivalent AML/CFT supervision, subject to conditions. However, the FA always remains ultimately responsible for the adequacy of CDD - responsibility cannot be fully delegated. Third-party reliance is not limited to institutional clients. MAS written approval is not required for each instance of third-party reliance.

questions.stem: The CPF MediSave contribution requirement for self-employed persons applies when their annual net trade income exceeds:
questions.explanation: Self-employed persons in Singapore must contribute to MediSave if their annual net trade income exceeds S$6,000. The contribution rate ranges from 4% to 10.5% depending on age. S$2,000 and S$4,000 are below the threshold. S$10,000 is not the prescribed threshold.

questions.stem: A representative discovers that a competitor has been making misleading comparative statements about her firm's products in client meetings. Under the ethics framework, the BEST initial response is:

options.A: Raise the matter with her firm's compliance or management so the issue can be addressed through proper channels
options.B: Make equally aggressive counter-claims about the competitor's products in client meetings
options.C: File an STR with STRO as the competitor's conduct may involve fraud
options.D: Contact the competitor's clients directly to correct the misinformation

questions.explanation: The appropriate response to a competitor's misconduct is to raise it through the firm's internal compliance or management channels, who can escalate through regulatory or industry channels if warranted. Retaliating with counter-claims perpetuates misinformation. Filing an STR is for money laundering/terrorism, not competitor marketing misconduct. Contacting the competitor's clients is inappropriate and potentially in breach of data privacy rules.

questions.stem: Under MAS Guidelines G04 on Risk Management of Internet Banking Services, financial institutions must implement controls to protect against unauthorized access. Which of the following is NOT one of the prescribed controls?

options.A: Multi-factor authentication for online transactions
options.B: Automatic session timeout after a period of inactivity
options.C: Real-time monitoring of all client transactions for pattern anomalies
options.D: Requiring clients to use only MAS-approved internet browsers

questions.explanation: MAS G04 requires multi-factor authentication, session timeout, and transaction monitoring as controls for internet banking. However, restricting clients to MAS-approved browsers is not a prescribed control under G04 - this would be technically impractical and is not an approach taken in the guidelines.

questions.stem: Under MAS Notice FAA-N06, Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) is required in all of the following situations EXCEPT:

options.A: When the customer is a PEP
options.B: When the customer is a Singaporean citizen with verified employment
options.C: When the transaction involves a country with known AML/CFT deficiencies
options.D: When the business relationship is conducted on a non-face-to-face basis

questions.explanation: EDD is required for PEPs, high-risk countries, and non-face-to-face relationships (among other high-risk factors) under FAA-N06. A Singaporean citizen with verified employment and no other risk factors is a standard-risk customer who requires ordinary CDD, not enhanced due diligence. Citizenship alone is not an EDD trigger.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST describes the concept of 'tipping off' under AML/CFT rules?

options.A: Providing unsolicited financial advice to a client without a prior engagement
options.B: Informing a client or third party that an STR has been filed or is being contemplated
options.C: Revealing a competitor's business strategies to clients
options.D: Disclosing a product's risk factors before the client asks

questions.explanation: Tipping off is the criminal act of informing a person who is the subject of an STR (or potential STR) that a report has been filed or is being contemplated, which could allow them to take steps to avoid detection. Unsolicited advice, revealing competitor information, and proactive risk disclosure are unrelated to tipping off.

questions.stem: Under the Code on CIS, a collective investment scheme that invests at least 70% of its net asset value in real estate-related assets and is listed on the Singapore Exchange is known as:

options.A: A hedge fund
options.B: A business trust
options.D: A special purpose acquisition company (SPAC)

questions.explanation: A listed CIS that invests at least 70% of its NAV in real estate assets and real estate-related investments is a REIT under the Code on CIS. Hedge funds are typically exempt from the Code. Business trusts operate differently under the Business Trusts Act. SPACs are acquisition vehicles, not income-generating real estate funds.

questions.stem: A client, Lim Beng Hock, aged 50, asks for a product to provide monthly income in retirement at age 65. He has low risk tolerance. Which of the following approaches is MOST consistent with suitability requirements?

options.A: Recommend a 100% equity unit trust because it provides the highest long-term return
options.B: Advise him to leave all savings in the OA to benefit from the 2.5% guarantee
options.C: Recommend a geared property investment fund to maximize income potential
options.D: Recommend an annuity or a capital-guaranteed retirement income plan aligned with his low risk tolerance and income objective

questions.explanation: For a client with low risk tolerance seeking retirement income, suitability requires recommending capital-protected or income-generating products such as annuities or guaranteed retirement income plans. Equity-heavy, geared, or property investments are inconsistent with low risk tolerance. While OA savings are safe, leaving all assets there ignores inflation risk and the income objective.

questions.stem: Under the framework for ethical behaviour, which of the following MOST accurately describes the difference between a 'rule-based' and 'principle-based' approach to ethics?

options.A: Rule-based ethics focuses on compliance with specific prescribed rules; principle-based ethics focuses on acting according to broader values even when no specific rule applies
options.B: Rule-based ethics requires advisers to follow MAS rules; principle-based ethics is optional
options.C: Principle-based ethics permits advisers to breach rules if the broader principle is satisfied
options.D: Rule-based ethics applies only to products; principle-based ethics applies only to client relationships

questions.explanation: Rule-based ethics involves complying with specific prescriptive rules; principle-based ethics guides conduct through broader values (such as fairness, honesty, and acting in the client's best interest) in situations where no specific rule applies. Principle-based ethics complements rules but does not permit rule breaches. Both apply across all areas of the business.

questions.stem: MAS Notice FAA-N06 requires financial advisers to adopt a risk-based approach to AML/CFT. What does this mean in practice?

options.A: Applying the same level of CDD to every customer regardless of risk factors
options.B: Filing STRs for all customers classified as medium or high risk
options.C: Allocating more resources and scrutiny to higher-risk customers and relationships
options.D: Refusing to serve customers from high-risk jurisdictions

questions.explanation: A risk-based approach means calibrating the intensity of CDD and ongoing monitoring to the assessed risk level of each customer relationship. Higher-risk relationships receive more intensive scrutiny. Universal application of the same level to all customers is inefficient and not a risk-based approach. STR obligations are triggered by suspicion, not risk classification alone. Refusing all high-risk-country clients is disproportionate and not required.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a correct statement about the CPF Retirement Account (RA)?

options.A: The RA is opened when a member turns 55 and is credited with savings from the OA and SA
options.B: The RA is opened for all CPF members from birth
options.C: The RA pays 2.5% interest guaranteed per annum
options.D: The RA may be used to pay HDB housing loan installments

questions.explanation: The CPF Retirement Account is created when a member turns 55. Savings from the OA and SA are transferred to the RA (up to the applicable retirement sum) at that time. The RA earns a minimum of 4% p.a. (not 2.5%, which is the OA rate). RA savings are designated for retirement income and cannot be used for HDB housing loans.

questions.stem: A client, Tan Siew Eng, aged 55, has the following CPF balances: OA = S$150,000, SA = S$120,000, MA = S$60,000. The Full Retirement Sum (FRS) at her 55th birthday is S$205,000. How much will remain in her OA after the RA is created?
questions.explanation: RA creation draws first from SA, then from OA if needed. SA = S$120,000 which is less than FRS of S$205,000. Shortfall = S$205,000 - S$120,000 = S$85,000 drawn from OA. OA remainder = S$150,000 - S$85,000 = S$65,000. SA is reduced to zero (all transferred). MA = S$60,000 is untouched. So OA balance = S$65,000.

questions.stem: Under MAS Notice 307, an insurer issuing an ILP must ensure that policy illustrations use a projected investment return of no higher than:

options.A: 4% per annum low scenario and 7% per annum high scenario
options.B: 3% per annum low scenario and 5% per annum high scenario
options.C: 5% per annum low scenario and 9% per annum high scenario
options.D: Any rate the insurer considers realistic based on past performance

questions.explanation: Notice 307 prescribes standardised projection rates for ILP policy illustrations: 4% per annum for the low scenario and 7% per annum for the high scenario. These rates are set by MAS to ensure comparability across products and to avoid misleading projections. Insurers may not use self-selected rates.

questions.stem: Under MAS Notice FAA-N06, a financial adviser must identify the beneficial owner of a legal arrangement (such as a trust). In which case must the FA identify the beneficiaries of the trust?

options.A: When the beneficiaries are named or identified, even if not yet holding any interest
options.B: Always, as all trust beneficiaries are treated as beneficial owners
options.C: Only when the trust has assets above S$1 million
options.D: Only when the trust makes a distribution to a beneficiary

questions.explanation: FAA-N06 requires identification of trust beneficiaries when they are named or sufficiently identified, because these individuals may be the ultimate beneficial owners. It is not limited to high-asset trusts, distributions, or post-distribution events. In class-of-beneficiary situations (where individuals are not yet identified), different rules apply.

questions.stem: A financial adviser firm's compliance officer discovers that three representatives have been signing client fact-find forms on behalf of clients without the clients' knowledge. Under the FAA and ethics framework, the compliance officer should FIRST:

options.A: Escalate the matter internally to senior management and the board, and consider whether a MAS notification is required
options.B: Report the matter immediately to MAS before any internal investigation
options.C: Issue the three representatives a written warning and require them to conduct additional CPD training
options.D: Immediately terminate the three representatives without further action

questions.explanation: The correct response is to escalate the matter to senior management and the board as a matter of urgency, and determine whether notification to MAS is required under the FAA's mandatory reporting obligations. Reporting directly to MAS before any internal investigation may not be appropriate as the first step; the firm must assess the situation. A written warning and CPD training are insufficient responses to a potential forgery issue. Immediate termination without following fair procedure may expose the firm to employment law liability.

questions.stem: Under the CPF framework, which of the following statements about Medisave is correct?

options.A: MediSave can be used to pay for any outpatient medical expenses without restriction
options.B: MediSave contributions are voluntary for employees above age 65
options.C: MediSave may be used to pay premiums for approved insurance schemes such as MediShield Life
options.D: MediSave funds earn a minimum interest of 2.5% per annum

questions.explanation: MediSave may be used to pay premiums for approved schemes such as MediShield Life, CareShield Life, and Integrated Shield Plans. MediSave for outpatient expenses is subject to withdrawal limits (not unlimited). CPF contributions including MediSave remain mandatory for employees below 65 (though reduced rates apply). MA earns a minimum of 4% p.a. (not 2.5%, which is the OA floor).

questions.stem: Under the FAA, a financial adviser is permitted to advertise its services. Which of the following is NOT permitted in an advertisement?

options.A: Stating the firm's MAS licence number
options.B: Providing contact details for the FA's representatives
options.C: Listing the range of financial products the FA is authorised to advise on
options.D: Including testimonials from past clients, without any disclaimer

questions.explanation: Under FAA conduct requirements and MAS guidelines on advertising, client testimonials must not create a misleading impression about the likely performance or outcomes of financial products or services. Using testimonials without appropriate disclaimers (e.g., that past experience is not indicative of future results) violates advertising standards. Stating the licence number, product scope, and contact details are all permissible.

questions.stem: A financial advisory firm is designing its compliance programme. Under the principles of sound compliance management, which of the following is the MOST important characteristic of an effective compliance function?

options.A: The compliance team must be the largest department in the firm by headcount
options.B: The compliance function must conduct at least 50 client audits per year
options.C: The compliance officer must hold a legal degree from a recognised university
options.D: The compliance function must be independent of business line management and have direct reporting access to the board or its audit committee

questions.explanation: An effective compliance function must be independent of the business lines it oversees and have direct access to the board or audit committee so it can escalate concerns without business pressure. Headcount size, academic qualifications of the compliance officer, and a specific number of client audits per year are not prerequisites for an effective compliance function. Independence and board access are the defining characteristics.

questions.stem: Under the Financial Advisers Act, a person who carries on a business of advising others on the purchase or sale of investment products without holding a valid financial adviser's licence commits an offence. Which of the following activities does NOT by itself require a financial adviser's licence?

options.A: Advising a client on whether to buy units in a collective investment scheme
options.B: Issuing a research report that recommends specific listed equities
options.C: Providing factual information on the features of an endowment policy without making a recommendation
options.D: Arranging for a client to enter into a contract for a life insurance policy

questions.explanation: Providing purely factual information about a product without making a recommendation is not financial advisory activity under the FAA and does not require a licence. Advising on CIS purchases, issuing research reports recommending securities, and arranging contracts for life insurance products are all regulated activities that require a licence or an exemption.

questions.stem: A financial adviser (FA) firm wishes to employ a candidate as a representative to market unit trusts. The candidate holds a valid Certificate in Investment Management (CKA) obtained 14 months ago but has not yet been appointed as a representative. Which statement best describes the CKA's validity status?

options.A: The CKA remains valid for 3 years from the date of passing
options.B: The CKA remains valid because there is no expiry date for it
options.C: The CKA has lapsed because it is only valid for 12 months if the holder has not been appointed as a representative
options.D: The CKA can be extended by sitting a refresher module within 6 months of expiry

questions.explanation: A CKA is valid for 12 months from the date it was obtained. If the candidate has not been appointed as a representative within that 12-month window, the CKA lapses and the candidate must re-sit the relevant examination. The 3-year period applies to the Customer Account Review (CAR), not the CKA.

questions.stem: Ahmad is a hired representative of FA firm Pinnacle Wealth Pte Ltd. He gives negligent financial advice to a client, causing the client to suffer a loss. Under the Financial Advisers Act, which party bears primary legal liability to the client?

options.A: Ahmad alone, as the person who gave the advice
options.B: Both Ahmad and Pinnacle Wealth jointly, with equal liability
options.C: Pinnacle Wealth Pte Ltd, as the principal of Ahmad
options.D: The Monetary Authority of Singapore, as regulator of the firm

questions.explanation: Under the FAA, the principal (the licensed FA firm) is vicariously liable for acts and omissions of its appointed representatives done in the course of carrying out regulated activities. Pinnacle Wealth therefore bears primary liability to the client. Ahmad may also face disciplinary action, but the firm's liability to the client is the primary outcome established by the Act.

questions.stem: A licensed financial adviser's licence is automatically revoked if the licensee is wound up or has its assets applied under a compromise with its creditors. Apart from automatic revocation, MAS may also revoke or suspend a licence on grounds that do NOT include which of the following?

options.A: The licensee has not carried on the business of providing financial advisory services for 6 months
options.B: The licensee's business is being conducted in a manner likely to be detrimental to clients
options.C: The licensee's paid-up capital has fallen below the regulatory minimum for 3 consecutive business days
options.D: The licensee failed to comply with any condition or restriction attached to its licence

questions.explanation: The FAA does not specify a 3-consecutive-business-day trigger for licence revocation based on capital falling below the minimum. The grounds for MAS-initiated revocation include ceasing business for 6 months, conducting business in a manner detrimental to clients, and failure to comply with licence conditions. A capital shortfall triggers different regulatory responses, but not automatic revocation after exactly 3 business days.

questions.stem: Which of the following individuals qualifies as an exempt financial adviser under the Financial Advisers Act without needing to hold a financial adviser's licence?

options.A: A sole proprietor advising retail clients on structured deposits
options.B: A remisier advising clients on unit trust purchases
options.C: A bank licensed under the Banking Act advising clients on investment products
options.D: A general insurance broker advising on investment-linked policies

questions.explanation: Banks licensed under the Banking Act are expressly exempt from holding a financial adviser's licence under the FAA when they provide financial advisory services. Sole proprietors advising retail clients, general insurance brokers dealing in ILPs, and remisiers advising on unit trusts are not within the statutory exemptions and would require licensing.

questions.stem: Representative Cheryl holds an appointment with FA firm TrueWealth. She recently passed her RES5 module but her employer has not yet submitted the appointment notification to MAS. A client approaches Cheryl and she provides financial advice. At the point of advice, Cheryl is best described as:

options.A: An exempt person because she operates under TrueWealth's licence
options.B: Duly appointed because she holds the relevant examination qualification
options.C: Duly appointed because her employer is a licensed firm
options.D: Not duly appointed and her advice constitutes an unlicensed activity by TrueWealth

questions.explanation: A representative is only duly appointed once the licensed FA firm has lodged the appointment with MAS through the MASNET/FAR notification process. Passing the required examination is a precondition, not the act of appointment itself. Until notification is lodged, Cheryl is not a duly appointed representative, and any advice she gives constitutes an unlicensed regulated activity attributable to TrueWealth.

questions.stem: Under the Financial Advisers Act, an appointed representative who is also an employee of the principal FA firm must comply with which of the following regarding secondary employment?

options.A: Secondary employment is prohibited entirely for the duration of the appointment
options.B: Secondary employment is permitted without restriction as long as it does not involve financial advisory services
options.C: The representative must obtain the principal's prior written approval before taking up any other employment or business
options.D: Only employment with another MAS-regulated entity requires approval from the principal

questions.explanation: An appointed representative who is an employee must obtain prior written approval from the principal FA firm before taking up any other employment or business activity. This applies broadly and is not limited to financial services employment. The rule prevents conflicts of interest and ensures the principal retains oversight over the representative's activities.

questions.stem: When a licensed FA firm appoints a new chief executive officer, the firm must notify MAS within how many business days of the appointment taking effect?

options.A: 5 business days
options.B: 14 business days
options.D: 7 business days

questions.explanation: Under the FAA notification requirements, a licensed FA firm must notify MAS of the appointment of a new CEO (or other key change in the management structure) within 14 business days of the appointment. The 7-day period applies to certain other notifications, and 30 days applies to changes in some corporate documents, so 14 business days is the correct threshold for CEO appointments.

questions.stem: FA firm Meridian Advisory intends to register a new foreign-related company as a related corporation to assist in cross-border advisory work. Which statement correctly describes an obligation that arises?

options.A: Meridian must obtain MAS approval before conducting any joint advisory with the related corporation
options.B: Meridian must notify MAS of the relationship within 14 business days of the relationship coming into existence
options.C: Meridian must ensure the related corporation holds a Singapore financial adviser's licence before any referrals are made
options.D: No notification is required as long as the related corporation is regulated in its home jurisdiction

questions.explanation: When a licensed FA firm enters into a related-corporation relationship, it must notify MAS within 14 business days. MAS does not need to pre-approve the relationship before notification, but the notification obligation exists regardless of whether the related corporation is regulated abroad. Making referrals to an unlicensed foreign entity may itself attract regulatory scrutiny, but the primary obligation here is the 14-day notification.

questions.stem: Darren is an appointed representative of licensed FA firm Atlas Capital. He decides to set up a personal website on which he posts investment commentary and product recommendations under his own name, directing readers to contact him at Atlas Capital. Which of the following best describes the regulatory position?

options.A: The website is permitted as personal expression and does not constitute financial advisory activity
options.B: The website requires a separate content-provider licence from MAS
options.C: The website is only permissible if Darren disclaims that the views are his own and not Atlas Capital's
options.D: Darren must obtain Atlas Capital's prior approval because the website constitutes marketing material issued by a representative

questions.explanation: Marketing materials and communications that constitute financial advisory activity or promote financial advisory services must be approved by the principal FA firm before publication. A personal website on which a representative posts product recommendations falls within the definition of marketing material, and Darren must obtain Atlas Capital's prior approval. A disclaimer alone is insufficient to satisfy the regulatory requirement.

questions.stem: A licensed FA firm may provide services in respect of which of the following products without needing any additional licence or exemption beyond its FA licence?

options.A: Term life insurance policies that are not investment-linked
options.B: Leveraged foreign exchange contracts offered to retail clients
options.C: Futures contracts traded on an approved exchange
options.D: Over-the-counter commodity derivatives

questions.explanation: A licensed FA firm's core scope covers life insurance policies (including term life) and other investment products listed under the FAA's Second Schedule. Futures contracts traded on approved exchanges, leveraged FX contracts offered to retail clients, and OTC commodity derivatives require separate regulated activity licences under the Securities and Futures Act. Term life insurance does not carry investment features that would push it outside the FA firm's permitted scope.

questions.stem: MAS is conducting an inspection of BrightPath Financial. The MAS inspector requests to see records relating to client recommendations made in the past 3 years. Under the FAA's conduct-of-business rules, the minimum record-retention period for such recommendation records is:

options.A: 5 years from the date of each recommendation
options.B: 10 years from the date of each recommendation
options.C: 7 years from the date of each recommendation
options.D: 3 years from the date of each recommendation

questions.explanation: Under the FAA's record-keeping requirements, an FA firm must retain records of its financial advisory business, including client recommendation records, for a minimum of 5 years. This 5-year period allows MAS to conduct inspections covering an adequate historical period. Records retained for only 3 years would not meet the regulatory requirement.

questions.stem: During an advisory session, representative Fiona tells a client that the balanced fund she is recommending has returned 12% per annum for the past 5 years and that similar returns can be expected going forward. The client relies on this statement and invests. If the fund subsequently underperforms, which ground is the client most likely to rely on to seek redress under the FAA?

options.A: Fiona failed to conduct a customer knowledge assessment
options.B: Fiona did not disclose the fund's expense ratio in writing
options.C: Fiona made a false or misleading statement inducing the client to enter into a transaction
options.D: The fund was not on BrightPath's approved product list

questions.explanation: Stating that past returns of 12% per annum can be expected to continue is a forward-looking claim that is misleading because past performance does not guarantee future results. Under the FAA (and paralleled by MAS Notice FAA-N03), a representative must not make false or misleading statements to induce clients to enter into transactions. This is the most direct and strongest ground for the client's complaint. The failure to conduct a CKA is a separate procedural issue and less directly linked to the client's loss.

questions.stem: Under the FAA, a licensed FA firm that contravenes the requirement to conduct its business with due skill, care and diligence is guilty of an offence and may be liable to a fine of up to:
questions.explanation: The FAA provides that an FA firm that breaches the general conduct-of-business obligations (including the duty to act with due skill, care and diligence) may be fined up to S$100,000 per offence. This is one of the key penalty thresholds that candidates must recall. The S$50,000 figure is associated with certain other FAA offences by individuals, and S$200,000 applies to more serious contraventions such as operating without a licence.

questions.stem: Representative Glen advises a client on an investment product but fails to inform the client about a significant conflict of interest arising from the fact that his firm receives a higher commission from that product provider than from competitors. Which MAS Notice is most directly contravened?

options.A: MAS Notice FAA-N02 (Dealings in Life Policies)
options.B: MAS Notice FAA-N16 (Balanced Scorecard Framework)
options.D: MAS Notice FAA-N03 (Recommendations)

questions.explanation: MAS Notice FAA-N03 on recommendations requires that before making a recommendation, the representative must disclose material conflicts of interest, including any commission bias towards a particular product or provider. FAA-N16 relates to the Balanced Scorecard remuneration framework, N11 covers managed accounts, and N02 deals with dealings in life policies. The conflict of interest disclosure obligation sits squarely in FAA-N03.

questions.stem: Under the FAA, which of the following is NOT a power that MAS may exercise when conducting an inspection of a licensed FA firm?

options.A: Requiring the firm to produce books and records
options.B: Entering the firm's business premises during business hours
options.C: Examining any person who is or was an employee of the firm
options.D: Arresting a director suspected of fraud

questions.explanation: MAS inspectors have broad powers of entry, production of books, and examination of persons connected to the firm. However, MAS inspectors do not have powers of arrest - criminal arrest powers are vested in the Singapore Police Force. If fraud is suspected, MAS may refer the matter to the police or the Commercial Affairs Department. The other options correctly describe powers available to MAS under the FAA inspection provisions.

questions.stem: Hui Lin is an appointed representative whose employment with FA firm Crestline is terminated. What is the maximum period within which Crestline must lodge the cessation of appointment with MAS?

options.A: 7 calendar days after the termination date
options.B: 14 business days after the termination date
options.C: 30 calendar days after the termination date
options.D: Immediately upon termination, before close of business on that day

questions.explanation: When an appointed representative's engagement ends, the principal FA firm must notify MAS of the cessation within 14 business days. This allows MAS to update the public register and prevents the former representative from being listed as active. Calendar days and same-day notification are not the correct standards under the FAA notification rules.

questions.stem: FA firm Nexus Wealth discovers that one of its representatives, Ivan, has committed an act of fraud against a client. Nexus terminates Ivan immediately. What obligation, if any, does Nexus have to report the matter?

options.A: No obligation to report; termination is sufficient
options.B: Nexyl must report to the Singapore Police Force only; MAS is not the relevant authority
options.C: Nexus must lodge a written report with MAS stating the facts, within 14 business days of becoming aware
options.D: Nexus must report only if the fraud involves more than S$5,000

questions.explanation: A licensed FA firm is required to lodge a written report with MAS whenever it terminates or accepts the resignation of a representative for misconduct (including fraud), within 14 business days of becoming aware of the facts. This obligation exists regardless of the amount involved and in addition to any criminal report the firm may make to the police. Termination alone does not satisfy the regulatory notification requirement.

questions.stem: Under MAS Notice FAA-N03, before making a recommendation on an investment product to a retail client, a representative must obtain the client's financial situation, investment experience and investment objectives. If the client refuses to provide this information, what is the representative required to do?

options.A: Proceed with the recommendation using general assumptions about the client's profile
options.B: Recommend only capital-guaranteed products to protect the client
options.C: Inform the client that the representative is unable to make a recommendation in the absence of the required information
options.D: Obtain written confirmation from the client's employer about his income before proceeding

questions.explanation: Under FAA-N03, if a client declines to provide the information needed to assess suitability, the representative must inform the client that without that information a recommendation cannot be made. The representative cannot substitute assumptions or limit the recommendation to capital-guaranteed products as a workaround. Seeking third-party confirmation of income is not a permitted response to the client's refusal.

questions.stem: The Balanced Scorecard (BSC) Framework under MAS Notice FAA-N16 requires that a representative's variable income be tied to non-sales KPIs. What minimum percentage of the total weightage must non-sales KPIs represent?
questions.explanation: Under FAA-N16, non-sales KPIs (quality indicators such as persistency, customer satisfaction and compliance record) must account for at least 40% of the total weightage used to determine a representative's variable income. If the weighting falls below 40%, the BSC framework's intent to counterbalance pure sales incentives is not met. The 30% and 50% figures are common distractors but are not the correct threshold.

questions.stem: Representative Jasmine earns a base salary of S$3,000 per month plus variable commissions. Under FAA-N16, for the BSC framework to apply to Jasmine's variable income, which condition must hold?

options.A: She must earn variable income in addition to a fixed component, regardless of the ratio
options.B: Her variable income must exceed 50% of her total income in any given month
options.C: Her variable income must exceed her fixed income in the most recent performance year
options.D: The BSC only applies if her variable income comprises 100% of her total income

questions.explanation: The BSC framework under FAA-N16 applies whenever a representative earns any variable income component tied to sales activities, regardless of whether the variable income exceeds 50% or 100% of total income. The distinction that matters for the 60% rule is between representatives who receive only variable income (no fixed component) versus those who receive both. But for the BSC to apply at all, the existence of any variable income linked to sales is the trigger - not a particular ratio.

questions.stem: Under FAA-N16, a Grade E is assigned to a representative in the BSC review. What is the automatic consequence for the representative's remuneration?

options.A: Variable income is reduced by 40% for the next review period
options.B: The representative's variable income is reduced to zero (full withholding) for the next review period
options.C: All variable income is withheld until the representative completes remedial training
options.D: The representative's appointment is automatically terminated by MAS

questions.explanation: A Grade E under the BSC Framework triggers full withholding of the representative's variable income for the subsequent review period - effectively reducing variable income to zero. Grade E is triggered if the representative has any Category 1 case (a serious consumer harm or misconduct finding). The FA firm does not automatically terminate the appointment, and MAS does not directly order termination under the BSC mechanism, though other disciplinary processes may run in parallel.

questions.stem: MAS Notice FAA-N11 on managed accounts requires that an investment mandate be documented in writing before any discretionary trading commences. Which of the following items is NOT required to be covered in the investment mandate under FAA-N11?

options.A: The client's investment objectives and constraints
options.B: The fee structure and basis for calculating management fees
options.C: The name and professional qualifications of the individual portfolio manager assigned
options.D: The benchmark index that the portfolio will be measured against

questions.explanation: FAA-N11 requires that the investment mandate cover the client's investment objectives and constraints, the fee structure, permitted asset classes and risk parameters, and the benchmark where relevant. The mandate does not need to name the individual portfolio manager or disclose that person's qualifications. Personnel assignments are operational matters and are not a prescribed element of the written investment mandate.

questions.stem: Under MAS Notice FAA-N16, a representative who received a Grade D in the previous BSC review period and then receives another Grade D in the current period is subject to which of the following consequences?

options.A: Full withholding of variable income, same as Grade E
options.B: A 20% reduction in variable income for the current period
options.C: A warning letter from MAS and a 12-month probationary review
options.D: Mandatory retraining only, with no impact on variable income

questions.explanation: Under FAA-N16, consecutive Grade D ratings escalate to the same treatment as a Grade E - full withholding of variable income for the next period. A single Grade D results in a partial withholding (claw-back), but two consecutive Grade D ratings trigger full withholding. This escalation mechanism is designed to address persistent quality concerns that fall short of a single Category 1 case.

questions.stem: MAS Notice FAA-N03 requires that a financial adviser provide a client with a product summary and a product highlight sheet (PHS) when recommending certain investment products. For a PHS, what is the maximum number of pages permitted?

options.A: 2 pages
options.B: 4 pages
options.D: 8 pages

questions.explanation: Under FAA-N03 and the associated product disclosure requirements, a Product Highlight Sheet must not exceed 4 pages. However, if the PHS includes diagrams or a glossary, up to 8 pages may be used. Where there are no diagrams or glossary, the strict limit is 4 pages. The question asks for the maximum permitted generally, which is 4 pages for a standard PHS.

questions.stem: A client contacts her adviser and requests to switch from a high-growth equity fund to a conservative bond fund within her investment-linked policy. Under MAS Notice 307, the insurer is required to process this switching request within how many business days of receiving all required documentation?

options.A: 10 business days
options.B: 3 business days
options.D: 21 business days

questions.explanation: Under MAS Notice 307, the insurer must process a policyholder's fund switching request within 7 business days of receiving all required documents and instructions. The 21-day period under Notice 307 applies to the insurer notifying MAS when establishing a new ILP sub-fund, not to processing switch requests. The 3-day and 10-day figures are not the mandated switching processing window.

questions.stem: Under MAS Notice 307, an insurer wishes to launch a new sub-fund under an existing investment-linked policy product. How much notice must the insurer give to MAS before the sub-fund can be launched?

options.A: 7 days
options.B: 21 days
options.D: 30 days

questions.explanation: MAS Notice 307 requires an insurer to notify MAS at least 21 days before establishing a new ILP sub-fund. This advance notification allows MAS to review the proposed sub-fund's investment objectives and compliance arrangements. The 14-day period is a common distractor, but 21 days is the correct figure in the Notice.

questions.stem: Under MAS Notice 307, an ILP insurer proposes to increase the management fee on an existing sub-fund by 0.15% of the sub-fund's net asset value per annum. This is considered a significant change. What notice must be given to existing policyholders?

options.A: No notice is required if the change is below 0.5% NAV
options.B: 14 days written notice
options.D: 1 month written notice

questions.explanation: Under MAS Notice 307, a fee increase of 0.1% or more of the sub-fund's NAV is classified as a significant change, and the insurer must give policyholders at least 1 month's written notice before implementing the change. The 0.15% increase meets the threshold for significance. A 3-month notice period applies in other regulatory contexts but not to ILP sub-fund fee changes under Notice 307.

questions.stem: An ILP sub-fund has a net asset value of S$50 million. During valuation, an error is discovered that caused the sub-fund's unit price to be overstated. At what minimum magnitude (as a percentage of NAV) does MAS Notice 307 require the insurer to compensate affected policyholders?

options.A: 0.5% of NAV
options.B: 0.25% of NAV
options.D: 2.0% of NAV

questions.explanation: MAS Notice 307 sets the valuation error compensation threshold at 0.5% of the sub-fund's NAV. If the pricing error equals or exceeds 0.5% of NAV, the insurer must compensate affected policyholders. Below this threshold, remediation is still good practice but not mandatory under the Notice. The 0.25% and 1.0% figures are plausible near-misses but are not the correct regulatory threshold.

questions.stem: Under MAS Notice 307, an ILP insurer identifies a valuation error that would require compensation to certain policyholders. For one policyholder, the compensation amount works out to S$15. Must the insurer pay this compensation?

options.A: Yes, all affected policyholders must be compensated regardless of amount
options.B: Yes, but only if the policyholder makes a written claim within 30 days
options.C: No, because the de minimis threshold is S$50 per policyholder
options.D: No, because the de minimis threshold is S$20 per policyholder

questions.explanation: MAS Notice 307 provides a de minimis threshold of S$20 per policyholder. If the compensation amount for an individual policyholder is less than S$20, the insurer is not required to pay it out. Since S$15 falls below S$20, this policyholder need not be compensated. The S$50 threshold is incorrect; S$20 is the figure stated in the Notice.

questions.stem: Under MAS Notice 307, the insurer must submit the audited accounts of an ILP sub-fund to MAS within how many months of the sub-fund's financial year-end?

options.A: 4 months
options.B: 2 months
options.D: 6 months

questions.explanation: MAS Notice 307 requires the insurer to submit audited accounts of each ILP sub-fund to MAS within 3 months of the sub-fund's financial year-end. The semi-annual unaudited accounts must be submitted within 2 months of the end of each half-year, but the full audited annual accounts require 3 months. A terminated sub-fund's accounts must be audited within 6 months of termination.

questions.stem: For an ILP policy issued on 1 September 2022, the insurer's marketing materials describe the front-end loading on premiums as a 'premium allocation rate' of 90%. Under MAS Notice 307, is this permitted?

options.A: Yes, as long as the 90% figure is clearly stated and the remaining 10% is itemised
options.B: No, because the premium allocation rate must be 100% for all new ILPs
options.C: Yes, as the prohibition only applies to ILPs issued before 8 October 2021
options.D: No, because the term 'premium allocation rate' is prohibited for ILP policies issued on or after 8 October 2021

questions.explanation: MAS Notice 307 prohibits use of the term 'premium allocation rate' for investment-linked policies issued on or after 8 October 2021. Because this policy was issued on 1 September 2022, it falls within the prohibition period. The correct approach for policies issued on or after that date is to disclose the actual charges on premiums without using that specific term.

questions.stem: MAS Guideline FSG-G01 sets out the fit and proper criteria for persons applying to hold appointments at financial institutions. Which of the following is NOT one of the three main criteria?

options.A: Honesty, integrity and reputation
options.B: Competence and capability
options.D: Financial soundness

questions.explanation: FSG-G01 identifies three main fit and proper criteria: (1) honesty, integrity and reputation; (2) competence and capability; and (3) financial soundness. Educational qualifications and professional membership may be relevant evidence under the competence criterion, but they are not a standalone fourth criterion. A candidate who confuses them as a separate criterion would give an incorrect answer.

questions.stem: Under MAS Guidelines for FA firms (FAA-G01), a new FA firm applying for a licence must demonstrate a minimum paid-up capital. What is the minimum paid-up capital required for a firm that intends to advise on and arrange life insurance products only?
questions.explanation: FAA-G01 sets the minimum paid-up capital at S$150,000 for FA firms providing advice on and arranging life insurance policies or securities-based products. The higher threshold of S$300,000 applies to firms dealing in futures contracts, leveraged foreign exchange, or OTC currency derivatives. S$100,000 and S$500,000 do not reflect the correct FAA-G01 thresholds for life insurance focused FA firms.

questions.stem: FAA-G01 requires that a new FA firm's chief executive officer and executive directors (EDs) collectively have sufficient industry experience. What is the minimum years of relevant experience required for the CEO, and what portion of that must include managerial experience?

options.A: 3 years total, with at least 1 year in a managerial role
options.B: 5 years total, with at least 3 years in a managerial role
options.C: 5 years total, with at least 2 years in a managerial role
options.D: 10 years total, with at least 5 years in a managerial role

questions.explanation: Under FAA-G01, the CEO (and each ED) must have at least 5 years of relevant industry experience, of which at least 3 years must be in a managerial capacity. This dual requirement ensures the firm's leadership has both depth of experience and management capability. The 3-years-total or 2-years-managerial options understate either the total or the managerial requirement.

questions.stem: Under FAA-G01, if a new FA firm does not have a 3-year financial track record at the time of application, which additional shareholding requirement applies?

options.A: The CEO must hold at least 10% of shares and the CEO plus EDs must hold at least 30%
options.B: The CEO must hold at least 20% of shares and the CEO plus EDs must hold at least 50%
options.C: All directors combined must hold at least 51% of shares
options.D: There is no additional shareholding requirement; the track record can be substituted by a performance bond

questions.explanation: FAA-G01 states that where a new FA firm lacks a 3-year financial track record, the CEO must hold at least 20% of the firm's shares and the CEO together with the EDs must collectively hold at least 50%. This requirement ensures management have meaningful skin in the game when there is no operating history to demonstrate the firm's financial stability.

questions.stem: Guideline FAA-G05 addresses independence in financial advisory services. Under FAA-G05, an FA firm whose revenue from a single product provider exceeds what percentage of total revenue is considered to have a commission bias that may compromise independence?
questions.explanation: FAA-G05 states that if more than 20% of an FA firm's total revenue is derived from a single product provider, MAS considers this indicative of a commission bias that may undermine the firm's independence. Similarly, if the firm represents fewer than 4 product providers, it may not be considered sufficiently independent to market itself as such. The 20% threshold is a key regulatory marker for independence assessment.

questions.stem: A Singapore-authorised CIS has a trustee that is related to the manager (cross-shareholding exceeds 20%). Under the Code on Collective Investment Schemes, which consequence follows?

options.A: The scheme cannot be authorised until the cross-shareholding is reduced below 20%
options.B: The scheme is exempt from the independence requirement if the cross-shareholding has existed for more than 3 years
options.C: The trustee must appoint an independent auditor to review transactions between the trustee and manager annually
options.D: The scheme is exempt from the trustee independence requirement if MAS pre-approves the arrangement

questions.explanation: The CIS Code requires that the trustee of an authorised scheme be independent of the manager. A cross-shareholding of more than 20% between the trustee and the manager fails the independence test. The scheme cannot be authorised in such circumstances until the cross-shareholding is reduced to 20% or below. MAS cannot waive this structural independence requirement, and longevity of the arrangement does not create an exemption.

questions.stem: Under the Code on Collective Investment Schemes, what is the maximum percentage of a CIS's deposited property that may be invested in securities issued by a single entity (the single entity spread limit)?
questions.explanation: The CIS Code sets a 10% single-entity spread limit - no more than 10% of a scheme's deposited property may be invested in securities or deposits of any single entity. A 20% limit applies at the group level (securities issued by entities in the same group). The 5% figure is associated with certain narrower restrictions, and 15% is not a standard CIS Code threshold.

questions.stem: The Code on Collective Investment Schemes prohibits a CIS manager from investing in securities of the manager itself or its related corporations, unless one condition is satisfied. What is that condition?

options.A: The investment does not exceed 5% of the scheme's deposited property
options.B: The trustee has given written approval for each such investment
options.C: The security is a constituent of a recognised benchmark index that the scheme tracks
options.D: Prior written consent has been obtained from a majority of unitholders

questions.explanation: The CIS Code prohibits a manager from investing scheme assets in securities of the manager or its related corporations, with one exception: the prohibition does not apply if the security is a constituent of a recognised benchmark index that the scheme is tracking. In that case, holding the security is necessary for index replication and not a conflict of interest. Unitholder consent and trustee approval are not the stated exceptions under the Code.

questions.stem: Under the Code on Collective Investment Schemes, the manager discovers that due to market movements a scheme has breached a spread limit (passive breach). Within what period must the breach be rectified?

options.A: 1 month from the date the breach is discovered
options.B: 3 months from the date the breach occurs
options.C: 6 months from the date of discovery, with MAS approval
options.D: Immediately upon discovery, with no grace period permitted

questions.explanation: The CIS Code allows a 3-month grace period for rectifying a passive breach of spread limits (one caused by market movements rather than an active investment decision). During this period, the manager must not make further investments that worsen the breach. Active breaches (where the manager's decision caused the limit to be exceeded) do not receive the same grace period.

questions.stem: A CIS manager receives soft-dollar benefits from a broker in exchange for directing trades to that broker. Under the CIS Code, which of the following conditions must be satisfied for the soft-dollar arrangement to be permissible?

options.A: The soft-dollar benefits must be disclosed to unitholders in the annual report only
options.B: The total value of soft dollars must not exceed 5% of total brokerage commissions paid in the same period
options.C: The soft-dollar benefits must be goods or services that directly assist the manager in investment decision-making, and the manager must act in the best interests of the scheme
options.D: The arrangement requires prior approval from the trustee and MAS

questions.explanation: The CIS Code permits soft-dollar arrangements provided the benefits are goods or services that directly assist the manager in the investment decision-making process (e.g., research, data services, trading systems) and the manager continues to act in the best interests of the scheme. Cash rebates are not permitted. There is no 5% cap on total soft-dollar value and no requirement for MAS pre-approval; however disclosure in periodic reports is required.

questions.stem: Under the Code on Collective Investment Schemes, the manager of an authorised scheme discovers a breach of section 289(3) of the Securities and Futures Act (scheme property held in trust). Within how many business days must the manager notify MAS?

options.A: 1 business day
options.B: 2 business days
options.D: 3 business days

questions.explanation: The CIS Code requires the manager to notify MAS of a breach of s.289(3) of the SFA (which relates to scheme property being held in trust) within 3 business days of becoming aware. This is a specific and important timeline. The 1-day and 2-day figures are not correct, and 5 business days would be too slow for this type of regulatory breach notification.

questions.stem: Under the SFA, section 197 prohibits false trading and market rigging. Which of the following activities best exemplifies a section 197 offence?

options.A: A director of a listed company trading in its shares after learning of a pending merger
options.B: A dealer spreading false positive news about a company to inflate its share price
options.C: A trader placing and cancelling buy orders repeatedly to create an appearance of active trading interest
options.D: An analyst issuing a research report with inflated price targets to benefit a fund the analyst personally holds

questions.explanation: Section 197 of the SFA addresses false trading - creating a misleading appearance of active trading or a false price. Repeatedly placing and cancelling orders (layering or spoofing) creates a false impression of demand without any genuine change in beneficial ownership, which is the essence of s.197 market rigging. Option (A) describes conduct closer to s.199 (false statements). Option (C) is insider trading under s.218-219. Option (D) could fall under s.201 or analyst conflict-of-interest rules.

questions.stem: Under the SFA's market conduct provisions, a 'wash sale' is a transaction that results in:

options.A: A sale of securities at a price lower than the current market price
options.B: A change in beneficial ownership but no change in the registered holder
options.C: A profit that is subject to capital gains tax
options.D: No change in the beneficial ownership of a security

questions.explanation: A wash sale under s.197 of the SFA is one where there is no genuine change in beneficial ownership - the same party owns the securities before and after the transaction. Such trades create a false appearance of market activity and are prohibited because they mislead other market participants about the level of genuine trading interest.

questions.stem: Under the SFA's insider trading provisions (s.218-219), when is a person who is a 'connected person' (as defined) to a corporation presumed to possess inside information about that corporation?

options.A: The connected person is rebuttably presumed to possess inside information without MAS needing to prove actual communication
options.B: Only if MAS can show direct communication of the information to that person
options.C: Only if the connected person traded in the corporation's securities within 48 hours of the information being generated
options.D: The connected person is irrebuttably (conclusively) presumed to possess the information

questions.explanation: Section 218 of the SFA creates a rebuttable presumption that a connected person (e.g., a director, substantial shareholder, or officer) possesses inside information about the corporation. MAS does not need to prove actual communication or knowledge - the burden shifts to the connected person to rebut the presumption. The presumption is rebuttable, not conclusive (irrebuttable), distinguishing it from the stricter standard sometimes confused with it.

questions.stem: Under SFA s.215, information is 'generally available' and therefore NOT inside information if it meets which condition?

options.A: It is observable or reasonably deducible by an ordinary member of the public without requiring special access
options.B: It has been discussed at a board meeting of the listed company
options.C: It has been reported in at least one local newspaper
options.D: It has been included in a quarterly earnings disclosure filed with SGX

questions.explanation: Section 215 of the SFA defines 'generally available' information as information that can be observed or deduced by members of the public in the ordinary course of their daily lives, without requiring privileged access. Information that requires special access, is board-confidential, or has not been publicly disseminated does not qualify. A single newspaper report or an SGX filing would qualify once published, but the fundamental test is public observability and deducibility.

questions.stem: FA firm Goldcrest receives S$200,000 in cash from a new client purportedly as an initial investment in a mutual fund. Under MAS Notice FAA-N06 (AML/CFT), what is the threshold above which a licensed FA firm must file a Cash Transaction Report (CTR) for a single cash transaction?
questions.explanation: Under FAA-N06 (aligned with MAS AML/CFT requirements), a Cash Transaction Report must be filed with the Suspicious Transaction Reporting Office (STRO) for any single cash transaction of S$20,000 or more. The S$200,000 payment clearly exceeds this threshold. S$10,000 and S$15,000 are common distractors but are not the correct CTR threshold; S$30,000 is also incorrect.

questions.stem: Under FAA-N06, an FA firm establishes a business relationship with a new corporate client. During customer due diligence (CDD), the firm discovers that the client is owned by a chain of shell companies across three jurisdictions and the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) cannot be identified. What must the firm do?

options.A: Decline to establish the business relationship or terminate an existing one
options.B: Proceed but limit the client to low-risk products only
options.C: Proceed with the relationship and file an enhanced due diligence report with MAS annually
options.D: Appoint an external auditor to investigate the corporate structure before proceeding

questions.explanation: Under FAA-N06, if an FA firm cannot identify and verify the ultimate beneficial owner through enhanced due diligence, it must not establish the business relationship, or must terminate an existing one. Proceeding with the relationship under any conditions when the UBO cannot be identified is prohibited. Filing enhanced reports or limiting product access are not acceptable alternatives when the identity verification requirement cannot be met.

questions.stem: Under FAA-N06, which of the following is a circumstance that triggers Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) regardless of whether other risk factors are present?

options.A: The client is a small business owner with annual revenue below S$500,000
options.B: The client is a Politically Exposed Person (PEP) or a family member of a PEP
options.C: The client requests to invest more than S$100,000 in a single transaction
options.D: The client declines to provide employment details

questions.explanation: FAA-N06 mandates Enhanced Due Diligence whenever the customer is, or is related to, a Politically Exposed Person (PEP). This is an automatic EDD trigger because PEPs are deemed higher risk due to their potential access to public resources and exposure to corruption. The other scenarios may warrant additional scrutiny depending on other risk factors, but they do not automatically require EDD.

questions.stem: Under FAA-N06, a Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) must be filed with STRO as soon as practicable after the FA firm forms a suspicion. Which of the following actions by the firm is expressly prohibited once a STR decision has been made?

options.A: Filing the STR without notifying the compliance officer
options.B: Recording the grounds for suspicion in internal compliance files
options.C: Continuing to transact with the customer on an existing facility while awaiting STRO guidance
options.D: Tipping off the customer that a STR has been or will be filed

questions.explanation: FAA-N06 (and the underlying Corruption, Drug Trafficking and Other Serious Crimes Act) expressly prohibits 'tipping off' - informing the customer or any other person that a STR has been or is about to be filed. Tipping off could compromise any investigation. Filing without notifying the compliance officer would be an internal governance issue but is not the statutory prohibition. Recording grounds for suspicion is in fact required by AML rules.

questions.stem: MAS Notice FAA-N06 requires FA firms to screen clients and transactions against designated lists. Which legislation authorises MAS to require FA firms to freeze assets of persons on the designated list?

options.A: The Income Tax Act
options.B: The Securities and Futures Act
options.C: The Mutual Assistance in Criminal Matters Act only
options.D: The Terrorism (Suppression of Financing) Act and the United Nations Act

questions.explanation: The legal basis for freezing assets of designated terrorists and entities in Singapore is the Terrorism (Suppression of Financing) Act and the United Nations Act (which implements UN Security Council sanctions). FA firms must comply with these statutes by screening and freezing without court order in respect of persons on the lists. The MAS Notice operationalises these obligations for FA firms.

questions.stem: Under MAS Notice FAA-N17, a financial adviser firm must conduct customer due diligence (CDD) when it suspects money laundering even if no business relationship is being established. This obligation arises at which transaction amount threshold?

options.A: S$30,000 or more
options.B: S$10,000 or more
options.D: Any amount

questions.explanation: CDD triggered by suspicion of money laundering or terrorist financing applies regardless of the transaction amount - it is not subject to any monetary threshold. The threshold-based CTR obligation (S$20,000) is separate. When there is suspicion, the firm must conduct CDD irrespective of whether a minimum transaction amount is involved.

questions.stem: MAS Notice FSM-N23 requires that a financial institution maintain records relating to its AML/CFT measures for at least how many years after the end of the business relationship or transaction?

options.A: 3 years
options.B: 5 years
options.D: 10 years

questions.explanation: AML/CFT record-keeping requirements under MAS Notices (including FSM-N23 and FAA-N06) mandate retention of CDD records and transaction records for at least 5 years from the end of the business relationship or the date of the transaction. This aligns with FATF standards. The 3-year period is too short, and 7 or 10 years is not the mandated minimum.

questions.stem: Under MAS Notice FAA-N19, an FA firm must obtain the prior written consent of a client before using or disclosing the client's personal data for marketing purposes. If the client subsequently withdraws consent, within how many business days must the firm stop using the data for marketing?

options.A: 30 business days
options.B: 3 business days
options.D: 10 business days

questions.explanation: Under FAA-N19 (which aligns with the Personal Data Protection Act obligations operationalised for FA firms), once a client withdraws consent for the use of personal data for marketing, the firm must cease using it for that purpose within 10 business days. This is the prescribed response period. Three business days is too short, and 14 or 30 business days exceeds the required period.

questions.stem: Under MAS Guidelines FAA-G09 and G10 on the use of customer information, which of the following purposes would permit an FA firm to share a client's financial information with a third party WITHOUT obtaining the client's prior consent?

options.A: Cross-selling products offered by a related company
options.B: Sharing aggregated (but identifiable) data with a data broker
options.C: Sharing information with MAS or a law enforcement authority pursuant to a lawful demand or court order
options.D: Providing the information to a business analytics firm for market research

questions.explanation: Under FAA-G09/G10, an FA firm may disclose client financial information without consent where required by law or pursuant to a lawful demand from a regulator or law enforcement authority, or under a court order. Cross-selling to related companies, market research, and data-broker sharing all require prior client consent. The legal compulsion exception is narrow and does not extend to commercial or analytical purposes.

questions.stem: Under MAS Guideline FAA-G14 on fair dealing for vulnerable clients, a 'selected client' is one who meets any 2 of 3 criteria. Which of the following is NOT one of the three criteria?

options.A: Is aged 62 years or above
options.B: Is not proficient in the English language
options.C: Has a net worth below S$100,000
options.D: Has not attained GCE 'O' or 'N' level education or equivalent

questions.explanation: FAA-G14 defines a 'selected client' as one who meets any 2 of the following 3 criteria: (1) aged 62 or above; (2) not proficient in English; (3) has not attained GCE O-level or N-level (or equivalent). Net worth below S$100,000 is not one of the three criteria. The guideline focuses on vulnerability arising from age, language, and education - not purely financial position.

questions.stem: For a 'selected client' under FAA-G14, which additional safeguard must an FA firm implement when making a recommendation?

options.A: Obtain a countersignature from an independent financial planner before any sale
options.B: Conduct the advisory session in the client's preferred language and have a witness present, and record the session
options.C: Refer the client to a licensed bank before proceeding with any investment
options.D: Limit the client to capital-guaranteed products only

questions.explanation: FAA-G14 requires FA firms to conduct advisory sessions with selected clients in the client's preferred language (using a qualified interpreter if necessary), have an independent witness present, and record the session. These safeguards protect vulnerable clients from misunderstanding or undue influence. There is no requirement to obtain a countersignature from an independent planner, refer to a bank, or limit products to capital-guaranteed options.

questions.stem: Under MAS Guideline FAA-G15, online distribution of life insurance policies became permissible from which date?

options.A: 31 March 2017
options.B: 1 October 2016
options.D: 1 April 2018
